A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LeanQuant and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original LLM quantization evaluations, efficiency measurements, ablations, MT-Bench comparisons and BERT quantization experiments on SQuAD.

after.justification: V3 retains original experiments and adds quantization comparisons, large-model results and inference-efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The specified affine search changes from enumerating endpoints through T/2-1 to a bit-dependent bound t: 0.2T, 0.3T and 0.4T for 4-, 3- and 2-bit quantization (Equation 7 and Appendix B). Algorithm 1 also corrects the error-buffer index from j-1 to j-i. The underlying weighted grid learning and GPTQ/OBQ integrations remain.

E1.justification: The represented datasets and language tasks remain C4, WikiText2, the existing zero-shot benchmarks, MT-Bench and SQuAD. Additional model variants and comparisons reuse this coverage. The revised allocation of benchmarks to the 405B model and new timing workloads change evaluation settings rather than introduce a new data domain or language task.

E2.justification: V3 adds QuaRot-RTN and QuaRot-GPTQ comparisons in Table 8, extending evaluation to rotation-based quantization. AWQ participates in the new grouped zero-shot comparisons in Table 9, whereas v2 reports it in the perplexity comparison. GPTQ is also added to the memory comparison in Table 4. Existing baselines are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix J introduces inference profiling on an A100-40GB GPU, measuring decoding throughput and prefill latency with 4096-token workloads and batch sizes 1, 4 and 16. New evaluations include grouped quantization, Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct and non-uniform quantization of the largest models. Table 3 replaces the 405B PIQA column with broader LAMBADA/MMLU evaluation, changing its average's composition. The affine search bounds are also revised.

E4.justification: V3 Table 12 adds an inference-efficiency analysis across batch sizes and decoding/prefill phases, exposing batch-dependent differences between LeanQuant and SqueezeLLM. The existing p sensitivity study, initialization ablation, fused-grid-learning-kernel ablation and loss-error plots are retained. The renamed robustness appendix largely restates v2's error-accumulation discussion.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. Existing point-estimate and MT-Bench win-rate reporting is retained, and the new experiments do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V3 adds large-model non-uniform results, QuaRot and grouped comparisons, GPTQ memory measurements and inference timings. Existing values also change: Table 1's affine 3-bit Llama-2-7B average changes from 52.84 to 50.42, and 2-bit Mistral-7B from 40.18 to 34.43. The LLaMA-7B non-uniform rows are revised in v2 Table 8 versus v3 Table 10, including LeanQuant's 4.05-bit average from 58.87 to 53.36. These are reported revisions; the changed search specification and 405B task mix preclude interpreting all differences as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Equation 7 revises the formally defined affine feasible set, and Equation 8 introduces its bit-dependent bound. The main loss approximation and quantization derivations remain unchanged. The inverse-Hessian removal identity moves from v2 Equation 4 to v3 Equation 9; it is not a new derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: loss-error-aware affine and non-uniform grids, accurate and compatible quantization, and scalability to Llama-3.1-405B using two 48GB GPUs in approximately 21 hours. Added experiments support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: V3 explains uniformly spaced initialization through the tendency of random or k-means++ initialization to undersample extreme weights. Section 3.2.2 and Appendix B newly discuss excessive range shrinkage, poor representation of extremes and the rationale for bit-dependent shrinkage limits. The existing interpretation of loss-error reduction and iterative grid robustness is retained.

D1.justification: V3 adds a LeanQuant code-access URL, explicit shrinkage settings, and documentation of a dedicated non-uniform CUDA inference kernel and exllamav2 affine kernels. Appendix J specifies hardware and workloads for the new timings. Existing calibration, baseline reproduction and quantization hardware instructions are largely unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendix M substantially expands the short related-work discussion into calibration-based versus calibration-free quantization, quantization-aware training, broader LLM efficiency techniques, and uniform versus non-uniform quantization. New cited works include QuaRot, SpQR, BitNet, OneBit, NUPES, Mr.BiQ and KV-cache compression methods. This broadens research positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: V3 extensively rewrites the quantization background and grid-learning explanations, relocates the p discussion and inverse-Hessian update, and reorganizes the appendices around added explanatory, shrinkage, inference and related-work sections. Publication headers, affiliations and acknowledgements also change. The explanatory restructuring extends beyond ordinary copyediting.

P2.justification: V3 adds the grid illustration in Figure 3 and new QuaRot, grouped-quantization and inference tables. Tables 2-4 gain rows or columns, and the 405B table is substantially restructured. Table 11 redisplays the memory comparison in transposed form. Existing loss-error and MT-Bench figures are retained with resizing, relocation or renumbering.

improvement.justification: V3 improves clarity and reproducibility through the explicit shrinkage specification, corrected pseudocode index, grid explanations and code-access information. New baseline comparisons and inference measurements provide useful evidence beyond v2's already extensive evaluation. The gain remains limited: several accuracy revisions lack an explanation of whether they reflect corrections or reruns, and the changed 405B task mix prevents direct comparison of averages. These limitations temper, but do not outweigh, the added documentation and evidence.
